verdict: 2026-07-26 10:04:42 PDT — The accepted AR-2 hybrid adjudication and AR-3 durable failure record are sound, and AR-1 now uses one fingerprint contract. I would retain this architecture, but three new contract defects should be resolved before future lenses copy it: run IDs omit part of row identity, the est-cost check is tautological, and the fingerprint misses executable-mode changes. Both drift linters pass, but they intentionally check wording rather than these semantics.

findings.title: Run IDs omit lens and altitude
findings.claim: The manifest correctly defines a run by `(row identity, unitId, pass)`, but constructs `runId` as `<scope>::<unitId>::p<pass>`. When later slices add another L1 lens over the same scope and unit, their run IDs, stable artifacts, finding IDs, and report provenance collide. This is latent in slice 1 but breaks the reusable fleet contract explicitly intended for lenses 2–4.
findings.alternative: Derive `runId` from the complete row identity: `<lens>::<altitude>::<scope>::<unitId>::p<pass>`, or from a canonical encoding/hash of those fields. Keep the structured fields alongside the identifier.
findings.win: Eliminates cross-lens artifact overwrites and ambiguous provenance with one canonical identity rule, requiring no per-lens collision handling later.

findings.title: Manifest cost validation compares a subtotal to itself
findings.claim: The manifest records carry no cost, while its “implied cost” is defined as `Σ in-scope estTokens` and compared with the plan's in-scope `estTokens` subtotal—the same row fields on both sides. The plan semantic check only verifies total equals row sums; it never verifies `row.estTokens = row.runs × per-run cost`. Consequently an approved plan with arbitrary internally summed prices passes both gates, so the accepted AR-3 est-cost check establishes no new invariant.
findings.alternative: Record the per-run token estimate as a structured plan constant, require every row's `estTokens = runs × tokensPerRun`, assign that cost to each manifest record, and compare the manifest-record sum with the approved in-scope subtotal. This does not require the declined unified run artifact.
findings.win: Turns a tautology into one enforceable pricing invariant and eliminates malformed-price plans and future per-lens cost arithmetic drift.

findings.title: Content fingerprint ignores executable-mode changes
findings.claim: The canonical stream contains only path plus `git hash-object` of file bytes. A tracked script can gain or lose its executable bit without changing that digest, so the engine can accept a target whose runtime behavior no longer matches the approved source state. This repo itself contains tracked executable scripts, making the omission material rather than theoretical.
findings.alternative: Define the fingerprint over a canonical, NUL-safe tracked-entry stream containing path, working-tree object type/mode (at least the executable bit), and content hash, with an explicit marker for tracked deletions; use the identical helper in planning and execution.
findings.win: Closes a fail-open source-identity path while preserving the accepted single-fingerprint mechanism; one canonical helper also removes duplicated shell-format assumptions.
